builds.howItPlays: You play a cheap unit every turn, and you can exhaust Renekton and give up two runes for 2 extra energy that only pays for units, so your bigger units arrive a turn early. You hold back Ambush units, which you can play mid-fight to a battlefield where you already have units, such as Inferna (2 cost) and Rengar, Trophy Hunter (5 cost, 6 Might), then cast Punch First (+5 Might for 1) to win the combat and take the battlefield.
builds.whyYou: You like attacking from the first turn and making your opponent answer your units before they can set up their own plan. You enjoy holding a unit back and dropping it into a fight your opponent thought they had won, and deciding each turn whether to spend two runes now for a faster board. You don't mind that your deck has few ways to come back from behind, because you plan to score most of your points before your opponent's expensive cards arrive. If quick games won by constant pressure and well-timed surprises sound fun, this Renekton suits you.
builds.ratingNotes:
Changed 2026-09-25 (re-rate from the Maintainer's deck picks, style "Ambush Renekton", which merges picks styles 1 and 4): label stays Aggro, and coordinates moved from 8.5/9/4.5/7 to 7/7/5.5/4 (pace/stance/complexity/variance), the mean of three scored decks. The old numbers came from launch-era guides (riftboundguide.com, riftstorm.gg, riftbound.gg), not scored lists. Variance fell the most, from 7 to 4: these lists run full sets of cheap units and pump spells, with no reveal or luck cards, so the 'high-roll' reading from launch does not describe them. I dropped those three guideUrls because they describe the launch/starter-era deck, not this list, and replaced them with the scored deck pages. deckListUrl was the bare /decks page and now points to the display deck. The style name comes from the picks.
Scored decks: https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/106d4061-5d29-47e2-ba48-8b58dc7df185 (MaskofMomentum, Barcelona RQ Best of Renekton, also reposted as Best of Singapore; pre-ban, x0.75) Aggro 7/7.5/5.5/4; https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/3c84d571-de16-4d6c-a34d-a3afa0000381 (Joe Cilo) Aggro 7/7/5.5/4; https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/e0e31af2-d363-4871-a8b7-2efe0f7bfcff (sugarbomb, Best Renekton, 5 likes, posted after the ban; swaps Kinkou Initiate, Pit Rookie, Irresistible Faefolk and Nidalee for Cleave, Mischievous Marai, Pyke and Falling Star) Aggro 6.5/6.5/6/4.5. tools.ts style: Aggro 7/7/5.5/4, mean of 3, labels Aggro x3.
Adjustments, the same on every sheet: Pace +1 (the Legend turns two runes into 2 energy for units, so units land a turn early); Stance +0.5 (that energy can only play units, which pushes the deck onto the board); Complexity +0.5 (the Legend trades long-term runes for tempo, and Renekton, Rage Fueled and Protective Sands want 4 or fewer runes, so you manage your rune count every turn).
Deciding cards: Pace, from cheap units (Inferna, Pit Rookie, Irresistible Faefolk, Mischievous Marai) and Noxus Hopeful (Legion, costs 2 less). Stance, from Punch First, Rampage and Cleave pumps plus Rengar, Trophy Hunter, who can be played to a battlefield with enemy units. Complexity, from Ambush timing (Inferna, Nidalee, Rengar) and rune management. Variance stays low with full sets of units and pump spells.
Legend ability: Reaction. Spend two runes and exhaust Renekton to add 2 energy, usable only to play units or pay for units' activated abilities.
Also played: https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/94d21e5d-8df3-4b9b-8003-c4a8cb885040 (Dragon Ramp Renekton, ratchetash, Midrange 2/4/6/7; Seals, Mobilize and Herald of Scales ramp into a Dragon curve); https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/92bc38cb-2a1b-445e-b5fa-fa8ac4fd74e9 (Low-Rune Brute Renekton, eriidanos's Sobek, Midrange 5.5/6.5/6.5/5.5; keeps fewer runes than the opponent to power up Forsaken Baccai, Oasis Raider and Renekton, Brute); https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/b5c67f08-647b-4e7c-968d-0405d8784efb (Seal Ramp Renekton, Riftlab's Vendetta guide list, Midrange 5/6/6/5; Seals pay for colours so it can sit on few runes and still land Eclipse Dragon).
Confidence: medium. Only one deck has strong evidence (MaskofMomentum's Best of list), and the other two are fair.
Reviewer: the three 'decks for' styles are Midrange and at least 2 from this Build on some Axis. The lead agent kept them as discovery decks rather than a second Build because each is a lone deck. If more low-rune lists show up, they may be worth a second Build.
